clue.text: Paper that comes out after the match?

definitions.text: Paper that comes out after the match?

parts.words: Paper that comes out after the match?
parts.note: the match is a wedding, not a sporting fixture, and the paper is thrown over the couple

explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests sport and a newspaper report afterwards; here it means a marriage, after which little pieces of paper are thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bits of coloured paper are thrown over newlyweds as they leave the wedding ceremony.

clue.text: Exposed lovers steal pass

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its covering, so lovers loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Lovers caught in the open snatch a quick pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exposed' looks like it means OVERT, but it strips the outer letters of 'lovers'.
explanation.definitionFit: When one car passes another on the road it overtakes it, so these are synonyms.

clue.text: Newspapers, on behalf of the nation, will take on university

indicators.note: take on means admit, so the university letter goes inside the word for on behalf of

explanation.surface: The press acting for the nation will engage with a university.
explanation.definitionFit: The press is traditionally called the fourth estate of the realm, after clergy, nobility and commons.

clue.text: Seethes, essentially stifling proposals

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the answer is held inside the clue words

explanation.surface: Someone fumes, in essence choking off proposals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' tempts you to take the middle of 'Seethes'; instead the answer spans both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Theses are propositions put forward for argument, so proposals in an academic sense.

clue.text: Area to the south of Channel Island state

indicators.note: in a down clue, to the south of puts the area letter below the island

parts.note: the Isle of Wight, IOW, is an island in the English Channel

explanation.surface: A region lying south of one of the islands in the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel Island' suggests Jersey or Guernsey; it is the Isle of Wight, an English island in the Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Neon, perhaps, damaged granite top of structure

indicators.note: damaged granite is broken up, so its letters are rearranged
top of in a down clue takes the first letter of structure

explanation.surface: A neon sign damaged the granite top of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble gas that barely reacts chemically, an example of this class.

clue.text: Most of jurors perhaps sleep

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a jury has twelve members, a dozen

explanation.surface: Several jurors nod off during the trial.
explanation.walkthrough: English juries have twelve members, hence a dozen jurors.
explanation.definitionFit: To doze is to sleep lightly, a near synonym.

clue.text: Reduction of French credit facility

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
facility means ease, as in doing something with facility

explanation.surface: Cutting back on a French bank's credit facility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Credit facility' reads as one banking term, but the two words work separately; facility here means ease, as in doing something with facility.
explanation.definitionFit: A decrease is a lessening, a direct synonym for a reduction.

clue.text: Being able to take everything in?

definitions.text: Being able to take everything in?

parts.words: Being able to take everything in?
parts.note: a being (creature) able to eat every kind of food, not someone who understands everything

explanation.walkthrough: 'Being able' reads as a phrase about capacity to understand; 'Being' is in fact a noun, a creature, and 'take in' means eat.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that eats both plants and meat consumes all kinds of food, so it takes everything in.

clue.text: List of options in June, maybe travelling west

indicators.note: travelling west says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone planning a June trip westward weighs up their choices.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word, but it is what signals the letters are concealed within 'June, maybe'. UNEM, read westward in an across clue, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's card listing dishes is a set of choices, and computer menus offer options too.

clue.text: Regret returning after training a true star as chef, perhaps

indicators.note: after places the reversed regret at the end, following the rearranged letters
training shapes and reorganises, so the letters of a true star are rearranged
returning means the word for regret is read backwards

explanation.surface: A star being trained up to cook regrets the whole thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' looks like part of the story about the star but tells you to rearrange 'a true star'; the reversed regret word then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef may own or run a restaurant, which is exactly what this person does; 'perhaps' flags the example.

clue.text: Broadcast from coaches with no international assignment

indicators.note: with no means the international letter is removed

explanation.surface: A report on coach travel lacking any international assignment.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio or television programme sent out is a transmission, the noun sense of broadcast.

clue.text: Male pride and the speed of sound upset some briefly

parts.note: Mach 1, written MACH I, is the speed of sound

indicators.note: upset means the shortened letters are knocked into a new order
briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Boastful men brag about breaking the sound barrier and upsetting people.
explanation.walkthrough: Mach 1 uses the Roman numeral I. SOME 'briefly' is SOM, and 'upset' rearranges it to SMO.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes an exaggerated sense of masculine pride and toughness.

clue.text: Neat look at wild flower

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: A tidy glance at a wild flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like an adjective meaning tidy; it is an archaic noun for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxeye daisy is a common wild flower of meadows and verges.

clue.text: Good knock dad! That's the spirit

parts.note: pa is another word for dad

explanation.surface: Someone cheers on their father after a good knock, perhaps in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's the spirit!' is an encouraging cry, but the spirit here is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an Italian brandy distilled from grape residue, a type of alcoholic spirit.

clue.text: Charges time lost by carnivals

indicators.note: lost by means the time letter goes missing from the carnivals word

explanation.surface: Carnivals running out of time face extra costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Payments demanded for a service are charges, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Slow and enjoyable breakfast dish (not cold)

indicators.note: not means the cold letter is left out

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A leisurely, enjoyable breakfast without cold food.
explanation.definitionFit: Funereal means as solemn and slow as a funeral procession.

clue.text: Praise the French, occupying Brussels after evacuation

indicators.note: occupying puts the French word inside the emptied city
an evacuated city has been emptied, so only the first and last letters of Brussels remain

parts.note: only its outer letters are kept

explanation.surface: A tale of French troops moving into an emptied Brussels, to acclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: An evacuated city is emptied of its inside, so only the city's outer letters remain to hold the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: To glorify or extol, as in giving blessings to God, means to praise.

clue.text: British European party argue excessively

parts.note: Labour is a major UK political party

explanation.surface: A British European political party argues too much.
explanation.definitionFit: To belabour a point is to argue or discuss it at excessive length.

clue.text: Only painful if changing sides

indicators.note: sides are right and left, so the R becomes an L

explanation.surface: It would only hurt if you switched sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sides' here are R (right) and L (left): swap the R in SORE for L.
explanation.definitionFit: A sole survivor is the only one, so the word means single or only.

clue.text: One puts one's suit in a case

definitions.text: One puts one's suit in a case

parts.words: One puts one's suit in a case
parts.note: the suit is a lawsuit and the case a court case, not clothes packed in luggage

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like packing clothes in a suitcase; the suit is a legal action brought in a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A party to a lawsuit presses their claim through court proceedings.

clue.text: Poor delivery from posh type — a couple of lines

parts.note: a nob is a posh or upper-class person
L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines give LL

explanation.surface: A posh person speaking two lines does it badly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a no-ball is an illegal delivery by the bowler, penalised with an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: An illegally bowled ball in cricket is a faulty delivery, hence a poor one.

clue.text: Poets needing English, for example in schedules

indicators.note: in places the example abbreviation inside the schedules word

explanation.surface: Poets need English, for instance, on their timetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of elegies, mournful poems, are a kind of poet.

clue.text: Film about Times worker still living

indicators.note: about means the film title goes around the times sign

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: A film about a Times employee who is still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' suggests the newspaper; it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant means surviving or still in existence, as of species or documents.

clue.text: Republican always criticises and produces repercussions

explanation.surface: A Republican politician constantly criticising causes ripples.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that echoes on has continuing effects, which is a figurative sense of producing repercussions.

clue.text: Rule out Doctor Who at last

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of Who

explanation.surface: Banning Doctor Who at long last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' reads as the TV series, but splits into Doctor and the last letter of Who.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto a proposal is to forbid or reject it, ruling it out.

clue.text: Ruminants may go north for grass

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: Grazing animals may head north for fresh grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grass growing in wet places.

clue.text: Unprotected firm with a question for nation

indicators.note: unprotected means without its outer covering, so firm loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A firm without protection is questioned about a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern country, so an example of a nation.

clue.text: Height of talent with student in place of power

indicators.note: in place of says the student letter replaces the power letter

parts.note: L stands for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A talented student rises to a position of power.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Altitude is elevation above sea level, a synonym for height.

clue.text: Daughter had dinner after school and set off

indicators.note: after puts the dinner word behind the school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A daughter ate dinner after school and then left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' looks like departing; it means triggering an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to make it explode, which is what this verb means.
